transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

To answer your question directly: no, this does not necessarily mean the motor is failing. The V15 Detect has an 'Auto' mode that automatically increases suction when it detects more resistance (like a thick rug). This causes the motor to ramp up speed (louder noise) and drain the battery faster for those few seconds, which is normal operation. Please turn the vacuum off and inspect the Laser Slim Fluffy floorhead. Look at the brush bar (the roller with lights) – does it spin freely by hand when you rotate it? Also, check if there is any hair or debris tangled around the ends of the brush bar that might be causing it to drag on the rug.

Thanks. Just to check, I'm using the Digital Motorbar head with the red and black brush bar, not the Laser Slim Fluffy one. There's no hair wrapped round the brush bar, it looks clean. I'm not sure how freely it should spin by hand, so I can't really judge that. There's also no burning smell, heat or sparks, and the screen shows no warnings.

Since there's no hair blocking the brush bar and you're using the Digital Motorbar head (which has its own motor), the sudden noise and battery drop on the rug are very likely the 'Auto' mode doing exactly what it should: detecting the resistance of the thick pile and ramping up suction. The screen flickering or changing numbers is also typical as the sensor recalibrates. However, to be sure the brush bar isn't dragging (which would cause extra load), please turn the vacuum off and remove the battery. Turn the floorhead over and try spinning the red and black brush bar by hand. Does it spin freely with just normal bristle resistance, or does it feel stiff/gritty? If it spins freely, this is almost certainly normal behaviour for a rug transition.

I'm not sure how freely it should spin, but it doesn't feel stiff or gritty to me. I'd rather not take anything else apart as it's under guarantee. The screen says 'Auto' in the middle, which I switched to from Eco about two weeks ago, and I only noticed this since then. Is that relevant?

Yes, that is entirely relevant and suggests this is normal behaviour. The 'Auto' mode uses a laser and sensor to detect dirt density; when it moves from hard tiles (low resistance) to a rug (high resistance), the vacuum automatically ramps up suction power to clean effectively. This sudden increase in motor speed causes the louder noise, faster battery drain, and the screen fluctuations you are seeing. Since the brush bar spins freely and there are no warnings or burning smells, your machine is working as designed. You do not need to report it for repair.
